history.dynasty: Parmar (feudatories of the Gurjara-Pratiharas) - per inheritage.foundation; contested
history.period: 9th-10th century CE (per inheritage.foundation); local tradition credits Adi Shankaracharya / the Pandavas - unverified
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Rishikesh town - it stands at 1,330 m on Neelkanth Temple Road near Yamkeshwar in Pauri Garhwal district, about 30-32 km by road from Rishikesh, at the confluence of the valleys of Manikoot, Brahmakoot and Vishnukoot (Pankaja and Madhumati rivers). Mythology holds this is the spot where Shiva drank the Halahala poison of the Samudra Manthan (churning of the ocean), his throat turning blue - hence 'Neelkanth', the blue-throated one. The shikhara and walls are carved with scenes of the Samudra Manthan; a Shivalinga sits in the sanctum with Nandi facing it, and a natural spring on the premises is used by devotees for a purifying bath. FOUNDING-DATE CONFLICT FLAG: inheritage.foundation attributes construction to the Parmar dynasty (9th-10th c., Gurjara-Pratihara feudatories); templeyatri.in credits initiation of construction to Adi Shankaracharya; local lore links it to the Pandavas. No primary source establishes the date - verify before use.

name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
town: Neelkanth (near Yamkeshwar; CSV town 'Rishikesh' is approximate - the temple is ~32 km away)
town_description: Neelkanth is the forested hill locality on the Neelkanth Temple Road above Yamkeshwar in Pauri Garhwal, ~32 km from Rishikesh, reachable by road from Ram Jhula/Lakshman Jhula or by a 12-14 km trek from Swarg Ashram. Rishikesh, the nearest major town, is the Yoga Capital of the World on the Ganges at the Himalayan foothills.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 65-70 km via Rishikesh; verify)
travel.road: 32 km by road from Rishikesh (22 km from Ram Jhula); taxis, shared jeeps and buses run from Ram Jhula/Rishikesh. A 12-14 km trek route from Swarg Ashram/Ram Jhula also reaches the temple (4-5 hours one way).

visitor_information.best_time: February to May and October to November (pleasant weather); expect very large crowds in Shravan (July-August) and on Maha Shivratri
visitor_information.opening_hours: TIMING CONFLICT FLAG: sources disagree - 5:00 AM-6:00 PM (manchalamushafir, bugyalvalley), 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (poojn, apnayatra), and 6:00 AM-9:00 PM (traveltriangle, pilgrimaide). Morning aarti ~5:30 AM and evening aarti ~5:30 PM per manchalamushafir. Confirm current hours before visiting. No entry fee.
